dossier.public_summary: The dip alternates between shallow and deep exactly as expected for an eclipsing binary folded at half its true 26.6-day period, and its depth both between TESS sectors and between individual transits varies wildly from zero to over 1%. Together this is best explained by a binary blend rather than a repeating 2.8 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by ~5 sigma (~2.4x in depth) and the odd-even difference persists in individual sectors, as expected for an eclipsing binary at twice the period (P=26.6 d) rather than two alternating planet sizes.
reasons.value: diff_sigma 5.072, depth_odd_ppm 3610 vs depth_even_ppm 8788, depth_ratio 2.4, sector_oe_max_sigma 5.341, sector_oe_sectors_over_3 1

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor ~70x from near-zero to ~1.3% within the same TESS-SPOC pipeline (sector 10 vs 63), rules out a single planet depth and indicates diluted/contaminated eclipses or systematics changing with sector/aperture.

Individual transits are highly inconsistent; the two deepest events dominate the folded signal and there are negative-depth outliers, consistent with the sector-to-sector blend/variability seen in odd/even, not with 7-8 repeatable planet transits.
reasons.value: transits 8, p_consistent 1.3344587913877248e-32, chi2 166.56 dof 7, share_of_top_3 0.895, outliers 14961 ppm (+7.4 sigma), 15544 ppm (+5.1 sigma), -1284 ppm (-6.0 sigma), -702 ppm (-5.3 sigma)

reasons.why: Low planet_rank (well below median planet 0.5 and planet-like threshold) supports the combined binary/blend pattern over a planet; shape v_sigma -2.071 and neighbours plausible_within_1px 0 do not outweigh the strong odd/even and sector-depth evidence.
